methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised over $1.0B to date. The transportation sector contains seven private peers—including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and The ePlane Company—but no directly comparable public companies and insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private benchmarks to support peer-median valuation.

Given data constraints, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $1.0B total capital raised as a baseline proxy and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. This single-method triangulation produces a median estimate of $1.9B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.2B reflecting ±15% sensitivity around the core result.

The $1.9B median is supported by standard stage-advancement mechanics but faces material uncertainty on two fronts: the absence of granular same-stage comparable data prevents calibration of the 1.9x multiplier to JetZero's specific risk profile and market position; and reliance on total raised as a valuation proxy assumes no significant secondary activity or down-round dynamics. Future rounds or additional peer data in adjacent transportation subsectors would strengthen conviction in this range.
